model_output.verdict: An Army logistics and maintenance leader whose results make the move to operations supervision easy to follow.
write_up: You make a strong case for operations supervision! Your Army roles show a progression from mechanic to platoon sergeant, with responsibility for people, equipment, maintenance and field logistics. The results give a recruiter a clear reason to keep reading.

The vehicle readiness line is your model: it shows the rate before and after, the time it took and the changes you made. Your education is clearly marked as in progress, and your supervisor goal is easy to find.

Let's add a little more detail to the field exercise line so a civilian recruiter can see what logistics support involved. For operations supervisor roles, your resume isn't likely to be the thing holding you back; the fit with each job and how competitive it is will matter too.

cards.line: - Planned and executed logistics support for a 600-soldier battalion during two month-long field exercises
cards.cannot_tell: The battalion and exercise lengths show how much was involved, but a recruiter can't tell what support you provided. Naming the work will help translate it for an operations role.
cards.example: Planned and executed [type of logistics support] for a 600-soldier battalion during two month-long field exercises
cards.question: What logistics support did you plan and execute for the battalion during those exercises?

cards.line: - Cut the unit's vehicle non-mission-capable rate from 18% to 6% in a year by changing the parts ordering process and the weekly maintenance schedule
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this one. It connects a maintenance problem to the parts ordering and scheduling work you did, then shows the change in terms a recruiter can understand.

fit.note: Your experience points toward operations supervision, particularly work involving maintenance, inventory and teams. Your in-progress supply chain degree adds to that direction without overstating a completed credential.
